# pid-file-holder

<!-- AUTOGENERATED:BEGIN — do not edit; regenerated by `./equin build` -->

## Plugin reference

- Description: Who holds a daemon's pidfile, judged by the pid it names, never by a probe that can be slow: judgePidFile({ text, mtimeMs }, { uid, executable, argvMarker, probe }) answers live (a process of this user running the daemon's executable with its marker — data dir, config file — as a whole argument), stale (no such process, another user's, or one of ours that started after the file was written: safe to remove), foreign (one of ours, not the daemon, running since before the file: never removed) or unreadable (no pid on the first line); psProbeArgv / readPsProbe are the ps call that answers the probe (uid, elapsed time, full argv), run by the caller.
- Core:
  - Exports (types):
    - `JudgePidFileOptions`
    - `PidFileHolder`
    - `PidFileRead`
    - `ProcessSnapshot`
    - `PsResult`
  - Exports (values):
    - `judgePidFile`
    - `psProbeArgv`
    - `readPsProbe`
